flux_evidence: Trainer tooling ticks over steadily (musubi-tuner 0.5.0 in July 2026, ongoing ai-toolkit PRs) and the legal layer moved concretely this cycle (UK creation-criminalization live 2026-02-06, FTC enforcement live 2026-05-19), but nothing this pass forces a section-level rewrite the way the 2026-08-23 census repair did.

findings.claim: SKILL.md L177 and nsfw-training.md §1 state flatly that swapping in an abliterated ("heretic") text encoder does not uncensor diffusion output, because refusal lives in output layers a text encoder never uses.
findings.reality: A Heretic-abliterated Qwen3-VL-4B encoder is now packaged for Krea 2 (DreamFast, ComfyUI) specifically because the stock encoder is a VLM that genuinely refuses — rejecting ~30% of prompted content — and abliterating it measurably increases the share of prompts that reach the diffusion model, unlike a classic CLIP/T5 encoder.
findings.fix_hint: SKILL.md ~L177 and references/nsfw-training.md §1 (the -p-e-w- quote block) — add an explicit carve-out: the myth holds for CLIP/T5-class encoders, but VLM-class encoders that perform genuine understanding-level refusal (Qwen3-VL on Krea 2, per the existing Ideogram exception language) are a documented exception.

findings.claim: publishing-and-likeness.md §2 says only "the EU, the UK and several other jurisdictions have their own versions, and state-level deepfake statutes are still arriving" with no specifics.
findings.reality: This is no longer vague: the UK's Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 made merely *creating* (not just sharing) a non-consensual intimate deepfake a criminal offence as of 2026-02-06; the EU AI Act now classifies unsafeguarded NCII-generation systems as a prohibited practice; at least 45 US states have an enacted deepfake law as of mid-2026; and the federal NO FAKES Act cleared the Senate Judiciary Committee in June 2026.
findings.fix_hint: references/publishing-and-likeness.md §2, closing paragraph — replace the vague sentence with the UK creation-criminalization date, the EU AI Act prohibited-practice classification, and the 45-state count, each dated and sourced.

findings.claim: publishing-and-likeness.md §2 states civil penalty exposure as "~$53,088 per violation" with no note on why it might change.
findings.reality: The figure is confirmed current for 2026, but not because it was re-adjusted: OMB cancelled the 2026 inflation adjustment for federal civil monetary penalties government-wide (missing October 2025 CPI-U data) and told agencies to keep 2025 figures, so this number is frozen rather than freshly indexed.
findings.fix_hint: references/publishing-and-likeness.md §2 penalty row — one-line footnote that the figure is frozen for 2026 pending the next CPI-U-based adjustment, so re-check it in early 2027.

findings.claim: nsfw-training.md §2 (already self-flagged [re-verify]) names NoobAI-XL V-Pred 1.0 as the most anatomically accurate option, requiring the v-prediction + Euler sampler combination.
findings.reality: 2026 community comparisons increasingly point to NoobAI-XL **Eps** (epsilon-prediction, not v-pred) as the better 2026 default for character/illustration work — cleaner output and better named-character recognition — without the v-pred sampler trap.
findings.fix_hint: references/nsfw-training.md §2 NoobAI-XL row — check whether Eps has displaced V-Pred 1.0 as the recommended variant and update the sampler-trap warning accordingly.

new_techniques.what: "Not All Layers Are Created Equal" (arXiv 2603.21884, March 2026) proposes LoRA²: per-layer adaptive rank during fine-tuning on a personalization subject, letting layers that need it grow rank while others stay cheap, tested across 29 subjects on DINO/CLIP-I/CLIP-T.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Directly bears on the skill's deliberately-bracketed rank disagreement (8-64 across families) by offering a mechanism-level answer instead of a flat number.

new_techniques.what: 2026 trainer comparisons report OneTrainer running roughly 1.4–2× faster than AI-Toolkit on identical hardware, driven by torch.compile and int8-quantized (w8a8) training enabled by default.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: A throughput gap this size affects which trainer to reach for on constrained hardware, independent of the existing validation-loss differentiator.

new_techniques.what: ostris/ai-toolkit's mid-2026 PR stream adds qfloat8 offloading, a dynamic memory manager, offline mode, and Krea 2 block-by-block quantization improvements.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Lowers the VRAM floor for training on Krea 2 and other newer bases with this trainer, relevant wherever the skill recommends ai-toolkit.
